clue.text: Small container for 19 across turned up — it may be full!

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word for the container is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pot is what jam is kept in, 19 across being JAM

explanation.surface: A small jar of preserve is inverted, with a warning that it might be brimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' acts only on the container, since this is a down entry read upwards. 19 across is JAM, part of the long linked quotation, and a full stop is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is the punctuation mark, so the word can be qualified by full.

clue.text: Make a killing, backing horse

indicators.note: backing means the word for the crime is written in reverse

parts.note: to make a killing, taken literally, is to murder someone

explanation.surface: A gambler hopes to clean up by betting on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make a killing' reads as winning big; here it is literal. RED RUM was a famous racehorse, three-times winner of the Grand National, Britain's best-known steeplechase.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Rum is the celebrated Grand National winning racehorse, so it is an example of a horse.

clue.text: Fruit is cut, prepared for 7

indicators.note: fruit that is prepared is chopped and arranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Some fruit is chopped up and made ready for the next day.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is TOMORROW, so 'for 7' means designed for the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Something futuristic is made with the future in mind, as if meant for the days to come.

clue.text: Writer has heart trouble, not in advanced state

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: not tells us the following words are taken away from the heart complaint

parts.note: angina is chest pain from heart disease
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: An author with a cardiac complaint is in no fit condition to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN and A from ANGINA, leaving ANG. 'state' looks like condition but is the definition: Penang is a state of Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is one of the constituent states of the Malaysian federation, an island state in the northwest.

clue.text: Sort of Pisceans assigned month for new daydreams?

indicators.note: sort of here means a sorted version, so the letters get rearranged
assigned ... for signals one letter swapped in place of another

explanation.surface: Fish-sign people born in a certain month tend to live in a world of fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assigned month for new' puts M in place of the N of PISCEANS, giving PISCEAMS, which 'Sort of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is retreat into fantasy, of which daydreams are an instance, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Note to keep quiet and get engaged

parts.note: me is a variant spelling of mi, the third note of the sol-fa scale
sh is the call to keep quiet

explanation.surface: A message telling someone to stay silent about becoming betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get engaged' suggests marriage, but means gears interlocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth mesh when they interlock, which is to engage in the mechanical sense.

clue.text: See 9
Possibly 1 so late

definitions.meaning: 1 down is STOP; something that has stopped, such as a clock or engine, may be described this way
late can mean deceased, as in the late king

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition refers back to 1 down, STOP, as in stopping dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopped machine is said to have gone this way, and the late are the deceased.

clue.text: Crazy Sue, Hitler and Major Tom on ward, dancing to Unprogressive Traffic song — a brave DJ, my tune to broadcast as the White Queen spoke

annotationWithheld.why: Linked answer as held lists THERULEIS, BUTNEVER, TOMORROW, TODAY, JAM, YESTERDAY (42 letters), but the clue and enumeration give the full 51-letter quotation with JAM three times and AND; the wordplay (anagrams of Sue Hitler, Major Tom on ward, a brave DJ my tune to, plus JAM YESTERDAY) cannot produce the stored letters.
annotationWithheld.clue: Crazy Sue, Hitler and Major Tom on ward, dancing to Unprogressive Traffic song — a brave DJ, my tune to broadcast as the White Queen spoke

clue.text: Speck of electronic dust? Show how you feel!

indicators.note: a speck of the word is just its first letter

parts.note: a mote is a particle of dust

explanation.surface: A tiny particle of electronic dust seems to be invited to express emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speck of electronic dust' reads as one phrase; 'Speck of' takes only the first letter of 'electronic'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display one's feelings, often theatrically.

clue.text: Concealed diamonds in a foreign land

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for the card suit goes inside the country

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
D is the bridge abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Gems hidden away in some distant country.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu, borrowed from French, means hidden or out of sight, as when lying in wait.

clue.text: Choir Dana organised like one on the Web?

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Dana arranged a choir in a way suited to the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Web' suggests the internet; it is a spider's web.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachnoid means spider-like, and a spider is a creature found on a web.

clue.text: Crooner follows hit with "The Rite of Spring"

indicators.note: follows means the singer's name comes after the word for a blow

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
Bing Crosby was the archetypal crooner

explanation.surface: A crooner's next release after a hit is a cover of Stravinsky's ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Rite of Spring' looks like Stravinsky's ballet, but is read as a seasonal ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambing takes place each spring on farms, so it is a ritual event of that season.

clue.text: Joely Richardson's playhouse?

indicators.note: the possessive ending says the actress's full name owns, and so holds, a theatre inside it

explanation.surface: Asking which theatre belongs to the actress Joely Richardson.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lyric is a West End theatre in London, apt for an actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lyric is a well-known London theatre, so it is an example of a playhouse.

clue.text: Bloodless tissue? About right, actually

indicators.note: about means the phrase for actually goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: in fact means actually

explanation.surface: Someone asking about bloodless tissue and confirming they have it right.
explanation.definitionFit: An infarct is an area of dead tissue caused by loss of its blood supply.

clue.text: Wolves are confused about new rule

indicators.note: about means the confused word surrounds the rearranged rule

parts.note: fogged means befuddled or confused

indicators.note: new signals the word rule is given in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Wolverhampton Wanderers are bewildered by a change to the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the word rule, and 'about' puts the confused word around it. Wolves is the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, but here means the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolves walk on four limbs, so the description of them as quadrupeds completes the sentence.

clue.text: See 9
The Herald's covering day out back in the capital

indicators.note: back means what remains is read in reverse
out means the abbreviation for day is removed

parts.note: a tabard is the tunic worn by a herald

explanation.surface: A herald's garment kept a day out of sight on the way back to the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: TABARD without D is TABAR, which 'back' reverses. Rabat is the capital of Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabat is the capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: See 9
See 9
Travels with Ashes holder, wearing jumpers

indicators.note: wearing means the young kangaroos have the vessel inside them like clothing

parts.note: joeys are young kangaroos, which jump
an urn holds ashes; the cricket Ashes trophy is a small urn

explanation.surface: A cricketer touring with the Ashes trophy, dressed in woollen sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' suggests sweaters (British for pullovers); it means kangaroos.
explanation.definitionFit: Journeys are trips from one place to another, which is what travels are.

clue.text: Single guy now ready for regular outings

indicators.note: regular outings means taking letters at even intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: An unattached man says he is now prepared to go out regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwed means unmarried, which is what single means of a person.

clue.text: Eric ate chutney's secret Indian plant extract

indicators.note: secret says the plant extract is concealed within these words

explanation.surface: Eric ate chutney with a mystery ingredient from India.
explanation.definitionFit: Catechu is an astringent extract from Asian acacia and areca trees, used in tanning and medicine.

clue.text: Writer flipped over opening to last part of play

indicators.note: flipped over means the word for the opening is turned backwards

parts.note: a slot is a narrow opening
taken as written

indicators.note: last part of takes the final letter of play

explanation.surface: A dramatist turned over the start of a play to its final act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped over' turns SLOT into TOLS. 'opening' looks like the start of the play, but it is a slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace.

clue.text: See 24
Editor's blown a valve

indicators.note: blown, as of something exploded, signals the letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: An editor has blown a valve, losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown a valve' suggests losing one's temper; a triode is a three-electrode vacuum valve.
explanation.definitionFit: A triode is a thermionic valve with three electrodes, used in early radio.

clue.text: Cook enters carrying very small bribe

indicators.note: carrying means the rearranged letters hold the word for tiny within
to cook figures or accounts is to fiddle them, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A chef comes in bearing a little bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges ENTERS, and that jumble holds WEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is an inducement or bribe offered to win favour.

clue.text: Small sum paid to US bum, carrying empty hamper for Mavis

parts.note: something bought for a song costs very little

indicators.note: carrying means the American word for backside holds the emptied basket

parts.note: tush is American slang for the buttocks

indicators.note: empty leaves only the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tiny payment to an American tramp who carries an empty basket for a woman named Mavis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps just the outer letters of hamper, and 'carrying' places them inside. 'Mavis' looks like a woman's name; it is an old name for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavis is an old poetic and dialect name for the song thrush.

clue.text: Agency model meets US bum

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
ass is American slang for the bottom

explanation.surface: An agency model is introduced to an American backside.
explanation.walkthrough: TASS was the Soviet news agency.
explanation.definitionFit: TASS is the Russian state news agency, formerly the Soviet one.

clue.text: On and off?

parts.note: a machine that is on is working, and someone off is departing; one word covers both states

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a riddle about something intermittent, but the one word means both working and leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A working machine is described as up and running in this sense, and someone departing is said to be on their way out in this sense.

clue.text: Stays in hospital

definitions.meaning: stays are ropes that brace a mast or tent
... is a famous London teaching hospital, so a patient there is in this one

explanation.walkthrough: Guy's Hospital is a major London hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes are the stays holding a tent, and Guy's is a London hospital.

clue.text: Tyneside has records for Scottish roots

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
EPs are extended-play records

explanation.surface: A region in northern England owns recordings of Scottish heritage.
explanation.walkthrough: Neeps is Scots for turnips (or swedes), as in haggis, neeps and tatties.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps are turnips in Scots, and turnips are root vegetables.
